quotes.text: Compression comes after placement, not before it. If a data stream has no reason to leave the plant, compressing it only creates a smaller unnecessary transfer.

takeaways: Factory cloud cost is driven by data movement across boundaries, zones, gateways and return paths, not just by storage.
Estimate volume from sample rate, payload size and retention rather than device count, and move data only when a named consumer needs it for a named decision.
Use an edge, site and cloud layer pattern: filter, aggregate and infer near the machine, and send governed operational facts to the cloud.
hook: Sending all factory data to the cloud looks cheap until egress, cross-zone traffic, replication and dashboards show up on the invoice. This episode shows manufacturing and cloud architects how to model the real cost of data movement and build an edge-first pattern that scales. You will learn which data should stay local and which earns a trip to the cloud.
